domain_reasoning: Most time goes into reading the case and drafting the letter or email, then logging it.
length_reasoning: A routine reply takes a few minutes; a claim-result or adjustment notice needing explanation of findings takes half an hour.
review_reasoning: The reviewer reads the case summary and the message and checks tone and facts against the account.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong reply causes a follow-up contact; a wrong claim-result or adjustment notice can have financial or legal consequences.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's policies, templates and account system, learned over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: Time goes into pulling data from test management tools and dashboards and charting it in spreadsheets or BI tools before writing up.
length_reasoning: A simple trend over one release takes an hour; a multi-release analysis with data cleaning takes most of a day.
review_reasoning: The manager reads the report and spot-checks a few figures against the source data; a typical one needs trends re-derived.
stakes_reasoning: A flawed trend analysis misdirects planning but is usually noticed and revisable; rarely causes direct loss.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's test suites, naming, and history of releases, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is looking up the account or order in the billing or order system and comparing it with the promised change.
length_reasoning: A simple check is a couple of minutes; one needing several systems or a follow-up contact takes about twenty.
review_reasoning: A supervisor opens the case and the account to confirm the change; typical needs one system check.
stakes_reasoning: A missed failed change leaves the customer's problem unresolved and causes a repeat complaint; money-related ones can cost more.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's account and order systems and resolution procedures.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into entering the defect, attaching evidence, and setting fields in the bug tracker.
length_reasoning: A clear defect takes ten minutes to write up; one needing reproduction narrowing, logs and video takes under an hour.
review_reasoning: A triage lead reads the ticket and may try the steps; a typical one needs reproduction.
stakes_reasoning: A poor report wastes developer time but is caught in triage; a missed severe defect can reach release.
context_reasoning: Needs the product's components, tracker conventions and developers, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, time goes into looking up rates in the billing system and processing the payment or setting up billing.
length_reasoning: A simple quote and payment takes a few minutes; a complex service with billing setup takes a quarter hour.
review_reasoning: A quality reviewer listens to the contact and checks the charge and receipt in the system.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong charge is usually caught at reconciliation and refunded, but larger amounts or wrong billing setup cause financial loss.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's rate schedules, billing system and payment rules, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Time goes into pulling records from billing and account systems and checking outside data such as weather.
length_reasoning: A simple complaint takes a quarter hour; one needing meter history, outside data and several systems takes two hours.
review_reasoning: A supervisor reads the finding and checks the key records behind it.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong finding leads to a wrong remedy or reply, reversible but costly; large disputed amounts can be higher.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's systems, tariffs, and customer history, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is selecting codes and typing the summary into the CRM record.
length_reasoning: Routine wrap-up takes a minute or two; a complex contact takes about six.
review_reasoning: A reviewer reads the record and compares it with the contact; short records need a glance.
stakes_reasoning: A poor record causes confusion for later agents but is cheap to fix.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's disposition codes and CRM conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, time goes into typing notes and actions into the account system.
length_reasoning: The whole contact lasts a few minutes for routine ones and up to twenty for complex ones.
review_reasoning: A reviewer checks the notes against a recorded contact, partly sped up.
stakes_reasoning: Poor notes cause confusion later but are cheap to fix.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's account system and note conventions.

domain_reasoning: Time goes into imaging, installing software, and setting up accounts through admin consoles and tools.
length_reasoning: A standard image takes under an hour; a specialised role setup takes three hours.
review_reasoning: A supervisor checks the setup against a checklist; a typical one involves checking software and accounts.
stakes_reasoning: Missing software or access is noticed by the employee and fixed; security misconfiguration is rarer.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's images, software catalogue and account processes, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Time goes into pulling data from the tracker and building counts and charts.
length_reasoning: A templated weekly report takes twenty minutes; an end-of-sprint report with blocker analysis takes two hours.
review_reasoning: A manager reads the report and checks a few counts against the tracker.
stakes_reasoning: A mistake misleads the team briefly but is easily corrected.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's workflow states, labels and project knowledge.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into installing and configuring systems, scripts and infrastructure configuration.
length_reasoning: A small environment from templates takes four hours; a large production-like one with data takes days.
review_reasoning: The lead checks configuration against the specification and runs verification; this takes longer for large builds.
stakes_reasoning: A mismatched environment invalidates performance results and wastes test cycles, and can mislead release decisions.
context_reasoning: Needs deep knowledge of production architecture and constraints, built over months.

domain_reasoning: The output is a written procedure document.
length_reasoning: A short procedure takes under an hour; a detailed compliance-grade one takes five hours.
review_reasoning: A reviewer reads the document and checks steps against the product or standard.
stakes_reasoning: Poor documentation causes rework; audit gaps can create compliance exposure.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's documentation standards and product knowledge.

domain_reasoning: The main output is a written evaluation after reading, comparing and testing options.
length_reasoning: A small upgrade takes two hours; a major product evaluation with testing takes days.
review_reasoning: The manager reads the report and checks the main claims and costs.
stakes_reasoning: A bad recommendation can lead to a costly purchase or poor tool, hard to reverse.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the employer's environment and needs, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is editing test code and running pipelines.
length_reasoning: A small selector change takes half an hour; large refactors take six hours.
review_reasoning: A code reviewer reads the diff and checks the pipeline results.
stakes_reasoning: A faulty script gives false results caught in the pipeline; masked defects can slip through.
context_reasoning: Needs the test framework, code base and product knowledge, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is reading a document and writing findings.
length_reasoning: A short document takes twenty minutes; a long technical specification takes three hours.
review_reasoning: The author or lead reads the findings and checks them against the document.
stakes_reasoning: Missed errors cause rework later; compliance documents carry greater risk.
context_reasoning: Needs the product and standards in use.

domain_reasoning: The output is a written standard or criteria document.
length_reasoning: A small criteria list takes four hours; a full standard with consultation takes days.
review_reasoning: Managers read the document and check it against practice.
stakes_reasoning: Poor release criteria can allow bad releases or block good ones; hard to reverse once adopted.
context_reasoning: Needs deep knowledge of the product, risks and organisation, built over months.
